### [S023.U1] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.5 CEMENT MATERIALS
- A. Cement shall be ordinary Portland cement conforming to IS 269 for all purpose unless specified differently. It shall be received in bags of 50 kg and each batch shall be accompanied with a test certificate of the factory. Also it shall be tested before use to ascertain its strength, setting time, etc. In no case shall cement that has been stored over 4 weeks be used unless tested as per the direction of the ER prior to use in the Work.

### [S023.U2] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.5 CEMENT MATERIALS
- B. Cement shall be stored in such locations so as to prevent deterioration due to moisture dampness. A dry and water proof shed shall be best suited for this. Bags shall be stacked on rigid water-proof platforms about 15 to 20 cm clear above the floors and 25 to 35 cm clear or away from the surrounding walls. The stack height shall not exceed of 12 bags. Stacks shall be so arranged that the first batches are used first, and (FIFO) that they permit easy access for inspection and handling.

### [S023.U3] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.5 CEMENT MATERIALS
- C. The following other types of cement may be used in Work if specified or with prior approval of the ER in writing purpose. Specialist literature shall be consulted for guidance regarding use of these types of cement.
1. 43 Grade ordinary Portland cement conforming to IS 8112
2. 53 Grade ordinary Portland cement conforming to IS 12269
3. Portland slag cement conforming to IS 455

4. Portland pozzolana cement (fly ash based ) conforming to IS 1489 (Part-I)
5. Portland pozzolana cement (calcined clay based ) conforming to IS 1489 (Pt -2)
6. Sulphate resisting Portland cement conforming to IS 12330

### [S024.U1] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.6 WATER
- A. Water used for mixing and curing shall be clean, reasonably clear and free from harmful quantities of silt, oils, alkalis, acids, salts, sugars, and organic matter that could be detrimental to the concrete or reinforcing steel, cause efflorescence / stains / deposits, affect the hydration process or otherwise interfere with hardening of concrete during curing. Potable water is generally considered satisfactory for use but shall be tested prior to use in the Work.

### [S024.U2] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.6 WATER
- B. Water shall be tested in accordance with IS 3025. Maximum permissible limits of deleterious materials in water shall be as given in IS 456 and Table --7.
- C. Suitability of water shall be ascertained by the compressive strength and initial setting time test as specified under:
1. Average 28 days compressive strength of at least three 15 cm concrete cubes prepared with water proposed to be used shall not be less than 90% of the average strength of three similar concrete cubes prepared with distilled water. Preparation and testing in accordance of IS 516.
2. The initial setting time of tests blocks made with proposed cement and water to be used shall not be less than 30 minutes and shall not differ by ± 30 minutes from the initial setting time of control test block prepared with the same cement and distilled water. Preparation and testing of block shall be in accordance with IS 4031
3. The PH value of water shall not be less than 6 and more than 9.
- D. Water storage tanks shall be such as to prevent any deleterious materials getting mixed into concrete.
- E. Water tested as above shall be approved in writing by the ER prior to use in the Work.

### [S025.U1] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.6 WATER > TABLE - 7 / PERMISSIBLE LIMITS FOR SOLIDS (IN WATER) > [TABLE] TABLE - 7 / PERMISSIBLE LIMITS FOR SOLIDS (IN WATER)
|                    | Permissible Limit, Maximum                                                   |
|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Organic            | 200 mg/l                                                                     |
| Inorganic          | 3000 mg/l                                                                    |
| Sulphates (as SO4) | 500 mg/l                                                                     |
| Chlorides (as C1)  | 2000 mg/l for plain concrete work and 1000 mg/l for reinforced concrete work |
| Suspended matter   | 2000 mg/l                                                                    |

### [S026.U1] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.7 ADMIXTURES FOR CONCRETE
- A. General: Admixtures shall conform to the requirements of IS 9103, ASTM C260, ASTM C10, ASTM C 595 or ASTM C 618. Use shall conform to the requirements of IS 456 and IS 9103. Calcium chloride and thiocyanates are not permitted. Provide only those admixtures which produce no detrimental effects on metal components such as form and composite decking, reinforcing steel, embedments and conduit. Admixtures, when combined with other ingredients used to produce the concrete, shall result in concrete having not more than the limits for soluble chloride ion content in the specified standards or 0.6 kg/m 3 of concrete. All structural concrete shall contain a water reducing admixture.

### [S026.U2] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.7 ADMIXTURES FOR CONCRETE
- B. Admixtures generally in use are classified as follows:
1. Accelerators
2. Retarders
3. Workability agents
4. Water -repelling agents
5. Air-entraining agents
6. Gas-forming agents.
- C. Admixtures are manufactured and sold under trade names. Product data for each admixture proposed to be used in the Work shall indicate its trade name, chemical composition, purpose of use, source, directions for use, dosage rates and the possible detrimental effects of under and over-dosage. It shall also indicate chloride and sulphate content. Product data for air entraining admixtures shall indicate the average expected air content in freshly mixed concrete containing when dosed at the manufacturer's recommended rate..

### [S026.U3] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.7 ADMIXTURES FOR CONCRETE
- D. Fly Ash: Shall conform to IS 3812 (Parts I and II) or ASTM C618, Class C or F except limit lignite ignition to maximum of 6% with maximum of (220kg/m 3 ). No additives or contaminants derived from the fly ash precipitation process that are detrimental to concrete (such as soda ash) are permitted. The fly ash producer shall have a minimum of 5 years' experience in the production of acceptable fly ash and shall maintain an effective quality control program to guard against contamination of the fly ash.
- E. Other Admixtures: Use only with the prior written approval of the ER. Do not use any admixtures which contain chlorides or sulphates.
- F. Compatibility of multiple admixtures, including fly ash, used in the same mix shall be certified

### [S027.U1] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.8 AGGREGATES FOR CONCRETE
- A. Coarse Aggregate
1. Coarse aggregate shall be natural materials such as stone, gravel etc-crushed, uncrushed or a combination thereof-obtained from approved quarries. Aggregate shall be hard, strong, dense, durable, clean and free from veins and adherent coating. It shall be free from soft, friable, flat, thin, elongated or laminated pieces and shall be roughly cubical in shape. It shall consist of coarse material most of which is retained on 4.75 mm IS sieve.

### [S027.U2] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.8 AGGREGATES FOR CONCRETE > A. Coarse Aggregate
2. Coarse aggregate shall not contain any harmful material such as iron, pyrites, coal, mica shale or similar laminated material or clay, alkali, soft fragments, sea shells, organic impurities etc. in quantities that can adversely affect the strength and durability of the concrete. In addition to the above, in reinforced concrete the aggregate shall not contain any material that might attack the reinforcement. The maximum quantities of deleterious materials in the coarse aggregate when determined in accordance with IS 2386 Part I and Part II "Method of test for aggregates for concrete' shall not exceed the limits provided in Table -- 8.

### [S027.U3] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.8 AGGREGATES FOR CONCRETE > A. Coarse Aggregate
3. Aggregate crushing value, impact value, abrasion value and soundness of aggregate shall respectively be in accordance with paragraphs 3.3, 3.4, 3.5 and 3.6 of IS 383.
4. Grading of coarse aggregate shall conform to the requirements in IS 383. See Table - 9.
5. Source of aggregate shall be an approved Government location. It shall be tested prior to the approval of the ER by an approved testing laboratory. In case available aggregates do not meet specific requirements of IS 383 or any other applicable specification, required processing shall be carried out by the Contractor at his cost. It shall be the duty of the Contractor to make sure that aggregate material received by him is from Government approve quarries and with fully paid royalties, taxes, duties etc. as may be in force from time to time for respective locations.

### [S027.U4] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.8 AGGREGATES FOR CONCRETE > A. Coarse Aggregate
6. Aggregate shall be stored in such a way that it does not get mixed with mud, grass vegetables and other foreign matter. The best way ensure this is to have a hard surface platform made out of concrete, bricks or planks. It should meet the approval of the ER.
7. Coarse aggregate shall have a minimum specific gravity of 2.6 (Saturated surface dry basis). Aggregate below this specific gravity shall not be used without the special permission of the ER.

### [S027.U5] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.8 AGGREGATES FOR CONCRETE > A. Coarse Aggregate
8. Once a specific source of supply of coarse aggregate is approved, the source shall not be changed without the prior approval of the ER.
- B. Fine Aggregate
1. Natural sand deposited by stream or glacial agencies as a result of disintegration of rock is the best form of fine aggregate. The fine aggregate shall confirm to following standards.

### [S027.U6] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.8 AGGREGATES FOR CONCRETE > B. Fine Aggregate
- a. For Plain And Reinforced Concrete: IS 383 Specification for coarse and fine aggregates from natural sources for concrete.
2. Can be obtained from crushed stone screening but often contains a high percentage of dust and clay. It tends to be flaky and angular. This type produces harsh concrete and should be avoided.

### [S027.U7] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.8 AGGREGATES FOR CONCRETE > B. Fine Aggregate
3. Sea sand shall not be used unless approved by the ER. If approved, the required treatment shall be done at the Contractor's cost.
4. Sand shall be hard, durable, clean and free from adherent coatings and organic matter and shall not contain any appreciable amount of clay. Sand shall not contain harmful impurities such as iron, pyrites, coal particles, lignite, mica shale or similar laminated material, alkalis, and organic impurities in such form or quantity as to affect the strength or durability of concrete. It should also not contain any material liable to attack the steel reinforcement.

### [S027.U8] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.8 AGGREGATES FOR CONCRETE > B. Fine Aggregate
5. When tested per IS 2386 Part I and Part II, deleterious materials in fine aggregate shall not exceed permissible limits given in Table -- 8.
6. Fine aggregate shall be thoroughly washed at site with clean fresh water such that the percentage of all deleterious materials is within the permissible limits laid down.

### [S027.U9] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.8 AGGREGATES FOR CONCRETE > B. Fine Aggregate
7. Grading of fine aggregate shall conform to IS 383 and shall fall within limits of one of the four zones given in table 4 of IS 383. See Table -- 10.
8. Damp and moist sand increases in volume and this effect is called bulking. Due allowance shall be made for this effect when preparing mixes based on volume measurements. Bulking effects shall be determined per IS 2386 Part III Appendix A. For rough guidance Table --12 gives the relation between moisture content and percentage of bulking.
